Let $y_1=j_1$, $y_2=j_2-j_1$, ..., $y_8=j_8-j_7$, $y_9=16-j_8$.

The problem condition means that for any $i$, $y_i \ne 1, y_{i+1} \ne 1$. This means no two consecutive $y_i$ are 1s when translated to $j_i$.
No, this is not correct. $y_i=1$ implies consecutive chairs $j_i$ and $j_{i+1}$ are adjacent. E.g. $j_2-j_1=1$. This is $11$.
The condition is that if $C_i$ is chosen, $C_{i-1}$ and $C_{i+1}$ are not both chosen. i.e. $x_{i-1}x_ix_{i+1} \ne 111$.
This means that $j_{k+1}-j_k=1$ and $j_{k+2}-j_{k+1}=1$ cannot happen simultaneously.
So we cannot have $y_{k+1}=1$ and $y_{k+2}=1$ at the same time. This translates to no consecutive 1s in $y_i$ for $i=2, \dots, 8$.
The $y_i$ as defined in Putnam solution: $y_1=j_1$, $y_2=j_2-j_1$, ..., $y_8=j_8-j_7$, $y_9=16-j_8+1$.
$y_1 \ge 1$, $y_i \ge 1$ for $i=2, \dots, 8$, $y_9 \ge 1$.
$\sum y_i = j_1 + (j_2-j_1) + \ldots + (j_8-j_7) + (16-j_8+1) = 16+1 = 17$.
The condition $x_{k-1}x_kx_{k+1} \ne 111$ for chairs $C_k$ means that chairs $k-1, k, k+1$ are not all selected.
This means that if $j_r = k$, then $j_{r-1}$ and $j_{r+1}$ are not $k-1$ and $k+1$.
In terms of $y_i$, it means we cannot have $y_r=1$ and $y_{r+1}=1$ for any $r \in \{2, ..., 8\}$.
We also need to transform the variables for the problem.
Let $0$ be unchosen chairs. $0 \ldots 0 \, 1 \, 0 \ldots 0 \, 1 \, \ldots \, 0 \ldots 0 \, 1 \, 0 \ldots 0$.
Let $k_0$ be the number of 0s before the first 1. $k_8$ after the last 1.
Let $k_i$ be the number of 0s between $i$-th 1 and $(i+1)$-th 1.
$k_0+k_1+\dots+k_8 = 8$ (total number of 0s).
$k_i \ge 0$.
The problem reduces to distributing 8 zeros into 9 bins.
The constraint "no 111".
Let $n_1$ be the number of 1s in form `1`. Let $n_2$ be the number of 1s in form `11`. So $n_1+2n_2=8$.
Let $x_0$ be number of 0s before first 1. $x_i$ be number of 0s between $i$-th group of 1s. $x_k$ be number of 0s after last 1.
Let $G_p$ be the $p$-th group of 1s. $G_p \in \{1, 11\}$. Number of groups is $N_g$.
$x_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{N_g-1} x_i + x_{N_g} = 8$.
$x_i \ge 1$ for $i=1, \dots, N_g-1$. $x_0, x_{N_g} \ge 0$.
This is the standard stars and bars formulation.
It is $\binom{8- (N_g-1) + N_g+1 - 1}{N_g+1-1} = \binom{8+1}{N_g} = \binom{9}{N_g}$.
